cases.question: Current AX-17 renal guidance in Germany?
cases.answer:
In Germany, the renal dose modification for AX-17 is as follows: Normal (eGFR >=90): 50 mg OD starting dose, 100 mg/day maximum, routine monitoring [E2]. Mild (eGFR 60-89): 50 mg OD starting dose, 100 mg/day maximum, routine monitoring [E2]. Moderate (eGFR 30-59): 25 mg OD starting dose, 50 mg/day maximum, recheck 2-4 weeks [E1][E2][E3]. Severe (eGFR 15-29): Specialist review starting dose, 25 mg/day maximum, enhanced monitoring [E2].

cases.question: Compare AE evidence in HN-204 and HN-311.
cases.answer:
In HN-204, treatment-emergent adverse events (AX-17 %) were: Nausea 12.7, Headache 14.0, Fatigue 15.3, Dizziness 16.6, Rash 17.8, and Transaminase elevation 19.1 [E1]. In HN-311, treatment-emergent adverse events (AX-17 %) were: Nausea 11.8, Headache 13.0, Fatigue 14.2, Dizziness 15.4, Rash 16.6, and Transaminase elevation 17.7 [E2]. Control % rates were identical for both studies: Nausea 6.0, Headache 6.6, Fatigue 7.2, Dizziness 7.8, Rash 8.4, and Transaminase elevation 9.0 [E1], [E2]. Treatment % differences (HN-311 minus HN-204) lie between -1.4 and -0.9 points, and control % differences are +0.0 points [E4]. The highest treatment % in HN-204 is transaminase elevation (19.1) [E4]. The highest treatment % in HN-311 is transaminase elevation (17.7) [E4].

Sources
[E1] HN-204 · HN-204 Clinical Study v1.0 · APPROVED · effective 2025-06-12 · p.11, Table 14
     https://storage.cloud.google.com/tredence-fde-1-medevidence-vks/raw/HN-204_Clinical_Study.pdf#page=11
